Subject: Telemetry spike / brief notification — request for IR plan and artifacts

Hi Priya,

We're Silverline's security team. On 2028-03-30 we observed a short-duration spike in token errors and a small set of anomalous client IPs calling our integration endpoints tied to Redwood. No confirmed data loss yet, but our SOC wants the following to complete a triage:

- Redwood Incident Response Plan (IRP) or runbook that would apply to this class of telemetry anomaly
- A sanitized telemetry extract (timestamps + relevant request metadata) for 2028-03-30, ideally CSV
- A short timeline of actions taken if you performed any containment/remediation

Can you point me to the IR docs and share a folder for evidence transfer? We have to present this to our risk committee tomorrow afternoon.

Appreciate a quick acknowledgement and an ETA.

Thanks,
Ethan Cole
Security Lead — Silverline Payments

Preliminary timeline (abridged):
- 2028-03-30 02:04 UTC: anomalous increase in 401/403 errors from a small IP cluster
- 2028-03-30 02:10 UTC: automated circuit-breaker reduced request concurrency to affected backend
- 2028-03-30 02:22 UTC: temporary token-rotation triggered for impacted control plane keys
- 2028-03-30 02:35 UTC: traffic normalized; monitoring alert cleared at 02:40 UTC

Next steps: Karthik will produce a short technical root-cause note and a draft postmortem for your review by 2028-04-03. If you need the CSV in a different format or further redaction, tell us which columns to remove.

Thanks for the quick turnaround — the CSV looks useful. A couple of follow-ups from our side:

- Can you confirm whether any of the request payloads included customer-sensitive fields (PII or payment tokens)? We need to verify no sensitive token material was logged.
- For the runbook: can you include the SOC 2 control references (CC6, CC7 equivalents) or SIG/CAIQ crosswalk so our compliance reviewer can sign off faster?
- Would you be able to provide a short statement on retention (how long you keep raw request telemetry) and whether the sample we received was trimmed for retention?

Also, can we get a short draft postmortem that includes proposed remediation and preventative controls? If possible, include expected dates for any configuration changes.

Ethan Cole
Security Lead — Silverline Payments

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>

Date: 2028-04-02T15:10:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Telemetry spike / confirmation of scope and draft postmortem

Ethan — quick technical answers inline:

- Sensitive fields: we validated that no raw payment tokens or PII were written to our telemetry exports. The CSV contains hashed client_ids and metadata only; payload bodies are not present. (We ran a pattern scan against the extract prior to sharing.)

- SOC 2 / SIG mapping: copying Neha who will attach the SIG crosswalk. In short, the relevant controls are included in our IR runbook and the mapping will be added to the postmortem draft.

- Retention: raw request telemetry is retained in our hot telemetry store for 30 days by default; aggregates are retained for 12 months. The CSV is an extract from the hot store and was trimmed to the 02:00–03:30 UTC window only.

- Root cause (draft): likely misrouting of a small subset of token refresh requests after a transient routing table update at the edge. This caused elevated 401s which triggered automated throttles. No evidence of credential compromise at this time.

Attached: postmortem-draft-silverline-20280403.docx (draft) — contains containment steps, corrective actions, and a proposed timeline to implement an additional pre-flight validation in our token routing (target: rolling deploy by 2028-05-10).

Karthik Iyer
IR Lead — Redwood Inference
karthik_iyer@redwood.com
(Attachment stub: postmortem-draft-silverline-20280403.docx)
